cards.text: Just then a man walks up to Jesus with the biggest question a person can ask: “Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?” No hello, no small talk, straight to ETERNITY.
Jesus catches that word "good" and hands it right back to him: “Why do you ask Me about what is good?” Friend, the man asked a question and got a question back, and I KNOW that feeling.

cards.question: Jesus asks the man why he's asking about what is good. What does Jesus say next about who is good?

answers.text: There is only One who is good
Anyone who keeps the Law is good

cards.question: Jesus tells the man that if he wants to enter life, he should keep the ___.

cards.text: The man wants specifics: “Which ones?” It's like your boss tells you to just follow the rules, and you're staring at a binder thicker than an oven door.
Jesus starts listing: don't murder, don't commit adultery, don't steal, don't bear false witness, honor your father and mother. And He's got one more.

cards.question: Jesus has one more commandment for the man after honor your father and mother. What is it?
After hearing Jesus' list, the young man says he has kept all of these commandments.
The young man says he has kept every commandment on Jesus' list. What does he ask Jesus next?

cards.text: Jesus tells him that if he wants to be perfect, he should go, sell his possessions and give to the poor. Friend, if that were me, I'd have to give away every chocolate chip in my bakery, and I'm sweating just SAYING it.

cards.question: If the young man sells his possessions and gives to the poor, what does Jesus say he will have?
Jesus tells the young man to sell his possessions and give to the poor. What does Jesus tell him to do then?
When the young man hears what Jesus tells him to do, he goes away in ___.
Jesus told the young man to sell his possessions. Why does the young man go away in sorrow?

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to His disciples. “Truly I tell you, it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.”

cards.question: Jesus gives a picture of how hard it is for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. What does He say would have an easier time passing through the eye of a needle?
When the disciples hear Jesus talk about the camel and the eye of a needle, they shrug it off as no big deal.
The disciples are greatly astonished at what Jesus says about the rich. What do they ask Him?

answers.text: Is it wrong to have wealth

cards.text: Jesus looks right at them and tells them that with man, this is impossible. Friend, it takes me five tries to get a THREAD through a needle, and I've got a mustache for hands, so I believe Him.

cards.question: Jesus tells His astonished disciples that with man this is impossible. What does He say about God?

answers.text: With God all things are possible
With God the rich must give more
With God only the poor get in

cards.text: Then Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, speaks up: they've left everything to follow Him, so what will there be for them? Peter just said the quiet part OUT LOUD, and honestly, I respect it.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples that in the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on His glorious throne, those who followed Him will sit on twelve thrones. What will they do there?

answers.text: Judge the twelve tribes of Israel
Rule over the nations of the earth
Guard the gates of the holy city

cards.text: Everyone who has left houses or family or fields for the sake of Jesus' name will receive a hundredfold. Friend, that's walking away from one cookie box and getting handed a HUNDRED.

cards.question: Everyone who leaves things behind for the sake of Jesus' name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit ___ life.
Jesus wraps up with one more line. He says many who are first will be last. What does He say about the last?

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin. Of its 9 choice cards, 6 are multiple choice (cards 3, 7, 9, 11, 12 and 14), 2 are fill in the blank and 1 is true or false.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin. Of its 7 choice cards, 5 are multiple choice (cards 2, 4, 6, 8 and 11), 1 is true or false and 1 is fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The joke fails the logic test. In 19:26, 'this is impossible' refers to a person being saved. The joke compares it to Papa Dorin threading a needle, which reuses the needle from the Bible image. Taking five tries also means threading is possible, so 'so I believe Him' doesn't follow. A baker would say 'huh?'

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action. One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting. It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: 'Peter just said the quiet part OUT LOUD' states as fact that the disciples had been privately thinking this question. The text never says so. The guess is not marked as Papa Dorin's own.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The Son of Man appears here for the first time, and the card doesn't say who He is (Jesus, speaking of Himself).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. The question says 'twelve thrones', and only the right answer repeats 'twelve' ('twelve tribes of Israel'). Also, 'Rule over the nations of the earth' is close in meaning to judging from a throne, so a baker could argue for it.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.
